rule_citation: Net metering: G.L. c. 164 secs. 138-140; 220 CMR 18.00 (as amended D.P.U. 21-100-A, D.P.U. 23-140-A/-C; D.P.U. 23-20-A); storage pairing D.P.U. 17-146-A (2019-02-01). Interconnection: uniform DPU-approved 'Standards for Interconnection of Distributed Generation' tariff filed by each EDC - NSTAR/Eversource M.D.P.U. No. 55D (filed 2026-04-09, effective 2026-05-01); Massachusetts Electric/Nantucket M.D.P.U. No. 1599 (issued 2025-05-06, effective 2025-06-01; cancels No. 1579 eff. 2025-04-15). MID-TRANSITION: IIRG proposed revisions to Simplified/Expedited process, system-modification costs and storage definitions docketed as D.P.U. 25-48 (investigation opened 2025-05-27); EDCs filed a joint Common System Modification (CSM) Fee proposal 2026-03-27 - outcome not verified.
applies_to: IOU only - NSTAR Electric (Eversource), Massachusetts Electric and Nantucket Electric (National Grid), Fitchburg Gas & Electric (Unitil). The 40+ municipal light plants (MLPs) are not DPU-jurisdictional for net metering or DG interconnection and set their own policies (see utility file).
nem_successor: No successor - net metering remains open subject to caps. DOER SMART 3.0 (225 CMR 28.00) production incentive is paid on top of net metering credits (SMART facilities cannot also generate SMART alternative on-bill credits and net metering credits for the same output).
nem_cap_res_kw: 60 (Class I, any generating technology incl. non-renewable, kW; AC basis not verified); no separate residential class
nem_cap_nonres_kw: 2000 private / 10000 public for solar, wind, anaerobic digestion (Class II >60 kW-1 MW; Class III >1-2 MW private, >1-10 MW public)
nem_aggregate_cap: General program caps: private 7% / public 8% of each EDC's highest historical peak load. Dec 2024: Eversource 408.24 MW private / 466.56 MW public; National Grid MECo 359.191 / 410.504 MW; Nantucket 4.069 / 4.650 MW; Unitil 7.167 / 8.191 MW. Cap-exempt: Class I renewable <=25 kW (nameplate cap exempt), and renewable Class I >25 kW / Class II / Class III serving on-site load with an ISA dated on/after 2021-01-01 (non-governmental). Cap allocations via MassACA. Current subscription level not checked.
export_credit_basis: 1:1 retail (standard credits: basic service + distribution + transmission + transition per-kWh; excludes customer charge, SBC/EE, demand charges); 'market net metering credits' for New Solar Class I >25-60 kW, Class II, Class III and cap-exempt on-site-load facilities = 60% of net excess generation (100% for municipal/governmental hosts) per Appendix A of each EDC net metering tariff
export_credit_value: Example: Eversource East R-1 Class I cap-exempt credit Aug 2024 ~27.607 c/kWh (basic service 15.772 + distribution 7.820 + transmission 4.052 + transition -0.037). Varies by EDC, rate class and month.
credit_rollover: indefinite (credits in $ never expire), except cap-exempt facilities serving on-site load, whose credits are cashed out or carried over each March at the EDC avoided cost rate (ISO-NE LMP-based); Class III / small hydro may be cashed out at EDC election
annual_true_up: None for standard net metering. Cap-exempt facilities serving on-site load: end of March annual cash-out/carry-over at avoided cost rate (220 CMR 18.05(5); D.P.U. 21-100-A p.48).
ic_standard: IEEE 1547 / IEEE 1547.1-listed equipment ('Listed' = passed IEEE 1547.1 tests); tariff definitions still cite IEEE 1547-2003 text; Eversource applies new inverter requirements to applications from 2023-10-01. Explicit IEEE 1547-2018 / UL 1741 SB requirement not verified in the tariff text read.
ic_fast_track_kw: No kW ceiling - Expedited Process covers Listed facilities that do not qualify for Simplified and pass Screens 1-10; failure moves to Standard Process
ic_simplified_kw: 25 (Listed inverter-based, single-phase on single-phase service or three-phase on three-phase service, radial circuit; area network: <=25 kW and <1/15 of customer minimum load)
ic_application_fee: Simplified radial: $0. Simplified network: $100 (<3 kW) / $300 (>3 kW). Expedited/Standard: $4.50 per kW AC, min $300, max $7,500 (Eversource MA application page; same figure reported for National Grid MECo M.D.P.U. 1579 - secondary; Unitil not verified). Pre-Application Report: $100 <250 kW, $250 250-500 kW, $750 >500 kW (pre-app prompted in PowerClerk at >=250 kW AC). Supplemental Review hourly charges not verified.
ic_study_trigger_kw: No fixed kW trigger - Supplemental Review / Impact Study when a screen fails or Supplemental Review exceeds 30 engineering hours; Group Study when multiple applications share a Common Study Area; ISO-NE Affected System Operator (ASO) study when an Affected System impact is identified (tariff timeframes pause during ASO Study)
insurance_required: Tariff Section 11 sets insurance requirements (self-insurance allowed, Sec. 11.4); dollar amounts by size not verified
ic_timeline_days: Simplified radial: 3 BD acknowledge, 10 BD review (20 BD if Screen 5 fails), 10 BD witness test after Certificate of Completion. Simplified network: 30 BD review once minimum load known. Standard ISA delivery tables: 100/125/160 days depending on complexity and whether system modifications < or >= $1.5M. Group Study ISA 15/25/35 days after notice period by group size.
storage_allowed: Yes-with-conditions - ESS interconnects under the same DG tariff. Adding ESS to an existing solar facility is expressly NOT a 'Facility expansion' under NSTAR M.D.P.U. 55D Sec. 3.5 (handled by ISA amendment, not an Expansion Amendment), but Simplified-process facilities that expand need a new Conditional Approval for the full capacity. Net metering eligibility of paired storage limited to configurations in D.P.U. 17-146-A. Adding ESS to an existing net-metered facility is allowed if configuration conforms to D.P.U. 17-146-A (report to EDC + System of Assurance); non-conforming = loss of NM eligibility and cap allocation (mass.gov Energy storage and net metering page). Host customer holds energy/capacity rights of the ESS (D.P.U. 17-146-B at 22).
grid_charging_allowed: Requires non-export - per DPU summary of D.P.U. 17-146-A (mass.gov 'Energy storage and net metering'): ESS that can export and charges from both the NM facility and the grid is NOT eligible to net meter; ESS that cannot export may charge from facility and grid and remain eligible; exporting ESS must charge only from the NM facility. Non-export configurations may inadvertently export max 30 seconds and such export is not compensated. Ineligible paired systems may still interconnect as a Qualifying Facility. Existing or new NM facilities adding ESS must report it to the EDC and the System of Assurance Administrator; a non-conforming paired system loses NM eligibility and forfeits its cap allocation. Source: https://www.mass.gov/info-details/energy-storage-and-net-metering
non_export_option: Yes-with-conditions - tariff recognizes an EDC-approved export limiting scheme for inverter-based generation plus integrated ESS ('Maximum Export Capacity'), used at least for Group Study common-system-modification cost allocation (Sec. 3.4.1(h)); 'changes to export/import control requirements' are not a Facility expansion. ConnectedSolutions non-export path not verified.

rule_citation: Net metering: R.I. Gen. Laws ch. 39-26.4 (secs. 39-26.4-2, -3; amended P.L. 2023 ch. 300/301 and P.L. 2025 ch. 256/269); RI Energy Net Metering Provision R.I.P.U.C. No. 2075 (as amended). Storage pairing: RIPUC Order No. 22991 (Docket 4743, 2017-12-22) and Docket 4982 declaratory ruling (Open Meeting 2019-12-17). Interconnection: Narragansett Electric d/b/a Rhode Island Energy 'Standards for Connecting Distributed Generation' R.I.P.U.C. No. 2258 (eff. 2022-09-01; still cited as current in Docket 25-24-EL, 2025-2026). MID-TRANSITION: RIPUC Docket 24-34-EL (Development of Tariffs Applicable to Energy Storage Systems Connected to the Distribution System, opened 2024) and Docket 5000 (storage as a distribution resource) - outcomes not verified.
applies_to: IOU (Rhode Island Energy / Narragansett Electric). Block Island Utility District and Pascoag Utility District are excluded from the statutory EDC definition and must offer net metering under their own RIPUC-approved tariffs (R.I. Gen. Laws 39-26.4-2(3)).
nem_successor: No successor - net metering open. For projects after 2023-04-15 subject to the 275 MWac cap under 39-26.4-3(a)(1)(vi) (ground-mounted remote systems), the renewable net-metering credit is reduced by 20% (39-26.4-2(22)); OER summarizes this as a 20% cut for projects initiated after 2023-04-15. Whether the 20% reduction reaches behind-the-meter rooftop systems (which are exempt from the 275 MW cap) not verified.
nem_cap_res_kw: 10000 (10 MW nameplate max for any eligible net-metering system); no separate residential cap
nem_cap_nonres_kw: 10000 (10 MW nameplate; virtual/remote NM for public entities, C&I, community remote also up to 10 MW)
nem_aggregate_cap: No aggregate cap on behind-the-meter NM. 275 MWac cap on ground-mounted remote NM systems (must be operating/under construction by 2030-07-01; excludes systems behind the customer's meter or serving same-owner contiguous accounts). Community remote NM 30 MW (legacy) plus redesigned OER community program 20 MW/yr up to 40 MW. Subscription level not checked.
nem_sizing_rule: <=25 kW nameplate: no sizing restriction based on prior consumption. >25 kW: reasonably designed to produce <= 3-year average annual on-site consumption (projected use allowed until history exists) (39-26.4-2(6)).
export_credit_basis: 1:1 retail up to 100% of billing-period consumption (renewable net-metering credit = last resort service + distribution + transmission + transition per-kWh charges; 80% of that for post-2023-04-15 capped projects). Excess >100%: 'excess renewable net-metering credit' at the ISO-NE energy clearing price per the current statute (OER page still describes it as the last resort service rate - statute text controls); for systems >25 kW, excess credit limited to 100-125% of usage; <=25 kW all excess eligible.
credit_rollover: Carry forward; EDC may elect to issue checks in lieu of credits, and may administer <=25 kW residential credits month to month with carry-forward. Customer may cash out any remaining balance after annual reconciliation at the lower of reconciled balance or current balance (39-26.4-3(a)(2),(4)).
annual_true_up: Optional: EDC may use a 12-month estimated billing plan reconciled annually; customer cash-out option after annual reconciliation. Month not specified in statute.
ic_standard: IEEE 1547 / IEEE 1547.1 'Listed' (tariff definitions still cite IEEE 1547-2003 terms); all Facilities must meet IEEE 1547 ride-through/VAr attachments and RI Energy ESB-756. Explicit IEEE 1547-2018 / UL 1741 SB date not verified in the tariff text read.
ic_fast_track_kw: No kW ceiling - Expedited Process for Listed Facilities on radial EDS that pass screens (spot/area-network Simplified candidates also go to Expedited)
ic_simplified_kw: 25 (Listed inverter-based, export capability <=25 kW, secondary service matching phase, radial EDS)
ic_application_fee: Simplified: $0. Expedited/Standard: $3/kW, min $300, max $2,500. Pre-Application Report: $100 <250 kW / $250 250-500 kW / $750 >500 kW (credited against application fee if applied within 15 BD). Expedited Supplemental Review up to 10 engineering hours at $125/hr ($1,250 max). Renewable Feasibility Study (in lieu of application fee): residential $0 <=25 kW / $50 >25 kW; non-residential $100-$2,500 by size. Impact Study/ISRDG: actual cost (deposits residential >25 kW $100; non-res $500-$10,000). R.I.P.U.C. No. 2258 Table 2.
ic_study_trigger_kw: No fixed kW trigger - Standard Process Impact/Detailed Study when screens fail; Pre-Application Report mandatory at larger sizes (>=250 kW threshold referenced); ISO-NE Affected System review can extend timelines
external_disconnect: Utility discretion - for Listed inverters the Company 'may require' an external gang-operated, visible-break, lockable disconnect (or comparable device by mutual agreement) at the PCC (R.I.P.U.C. No. 2258 Sec. 4.2.4(b))
insurance_required: Tariff Section 10 (General Liability, Insurer Requirements, Evidence of Insurance) - dollar amounts not read (text truncated)
ic_timeline_days: Simplified: 3 BD acknowledge, 10 BD completeness, 10 BD screen review (+30 BD supplemental), total 20/50 days to ISA; 10 BD witness test after Certificate of Completion. Expedited: 25 BD screens, 45/65 days total. Standard: 135/155 days (175/200 calendar if Detailed Study). System Modifications for renewables: 270/360 calendar days (substation). R.I.P.U.C. No. 2258 Table 1.
storage_allowed: Yes-with-conditions - ESS may be part of a Facility under R.I.P.U.C. No. 2258 (Nameplate Rating includes ESS; Simplified/Expedited eligibility requires all generating and ESS equipment be non-rotating inverter-based with UL-listed export-limiting components). Net metering eligibility of paired storage: RIPUC Order 22991 (<=25 kW AC solar+battery) and Docket 4982 ruling (all sizes) - battery charged only from the renewable system, host not on TOU rates, no claim to capacity/ancillary-service values, whole system behind the retail meter. Adding a battery does not change the NM system size (Order 22991 at 5-6: capacity = PV inverter rating). Standalone-storage tariffs pending in Docket 24-34-EL.
grid_charging_allowed: No - for net-metered paired systems, the battery must charge only from the solar/renewable generator; RIPUC Docket 4982 (2019-12-17) gave RI Energy the right to inspect to ensure 'no charging of the storage unit from the electric grid'. Export of battery discharge is allowed (Order 22991 struck the no-discharge condition). Grid-charged storage would fall outside net metering (treatment as standalone storage pending Docket 24-34-EL).
non_export_option: Yes - R.I.P.U.C. No. 2258 Sec. 4.3 'Limited-Export and Non-Exporting Facilities' (power limiting via protective functions, reduced rating, mutually agreed means; Power Control Systems allowed, may not assume a minimum site load); Export Capacity (not Nameplate) used for screening when limited by acceptable means
storage_counts_toward_cap: No - RIPUC Order 22991: solar+storage capacity equals the PV inverter nameplate; adding a battery does not alter system size for NM sizing. (Interconnection Nameplate Rating does include ESS.)
standby_charge: Statute requires RIPUC to exempt accounts with an eligible net-metering system from back-up or standby rates commensurate with the NM system size (39-26.4-3(b)); NM accounts otherwise keep their normal class rates incl. customer and demand charges.

rule_citation: Export comp: Residential Renewable Energy Solutions (RRES) created by P.A. 19-35 (C.G.S. 16-244z); RRES Program Manual v2024.1 (Docket 23-08-02 Order 18, eff. 2024-01-01); annual rate setting dockets (21-08-02, 22-08-02, 23-08-02 and successors). Legacy net metering closed to new applications after 2021-12-31. Interconnection: Eversource/UI joint 'Guidelines for the Interconnection of Residential Single Phase Certified Inverter-Based Generating Facilities of 25 kW(ac) or Less' (Docket 03-01-15RE04, rev. 2022-12-06) and 'Guidelines for Generator Interconnection Fast Track and Study Process' (Docket 17-12-03RE06). Storage incentive: Energy Storage Solutions (Docket 17-12-03RE03, 2021-07-28; redesigned for applications on/after 2026-04-01). MID-TRANSITION: PURA flexible interconnection proceeding (Docket 25-01-27, technical meeting 2026-03); RRES/NRES statutory program window (reported to end with 2027 applications) not verified.
applies_to: IOU only (Connecticut Light & Power d/b/a Eversource, United Illuminating). Municipal utilities (e.g., Wallingford, Norwich, Bozrah, Groton, Norwalk, Lebanon territories) are outside these EDC guidelines/programs and set their own rules.
nem_successor: RRES (applications from 2022-01-01), 20-year term, customer chooses once (cannot switch): (1) Netting Tariff - monthly netting, net excess credited at the full retail rate (standard service supply + delivery) plus a production-meter REC $/kWh (2026 base $0.000 plus adders) and, for 2026 enrollees, a non-bypassable Solar Energy Adjustment charge on production ($0.0402/kWh per Eversource 2026 rate table); (2) Buy-All Tariff - utility buys 100% of production at a fixed 20-yr rate (2026: $0.3289/kWh; 2025: $0.3195; 2024: $0.3189) with income-eligible and distressed-municipality adders. Legacy net-metering customers stay on NM until the PV system is removed (RRES FAQ Q72). Non-residential >25 kW: NRES competitive procurement (details not verified).
nem_cap_res_kw: 25 (kW AC inverter nameplate, total for all qualified systems on a 1-4 unit premise; co-located/paired storage capacity does NOT count toward the 25 kW cap)
nem_cap_nonres_kw: Not covered by RRES; >25 kW goes to NRES procurement (limits not verified)
nem_aggregate_cap: Annual rate setting targets roughly 50-60 MW/yr of residential deployment (RRES manual); no hard aggregate cap verified
nem_sizing_rule: Expected annual production <= highest consecutive-12-month consumption in last 5 years (+5% variance) plus allowances for up to two EVs (3,285 kWh each) and a whole-home heat pump (ASHP 3,608 / GSHP 2,458 kWh); <12 months history or new construction: up to 9 kW AC without usage showing
export_credit_basis: Netting: 1:1 retail (monthly net excess at retail rate incl. standard-service supply) less Solar Energy Adjustment on total production for 2026 enrollees. Buy-All: fixed $/kWh for all production (includes RECs).
export_credit_value: Buy-All 2026 $0.3289/kWh (+$0.055 income-eligible, +$0.0275 distressed municipality). Netting 2026: retail rate for net excess; REC $0.000 base (+$0.035 income-eligible, +$0.0175 distressed); Solar Energy Adjustment $0.0402/kWh of production (Eversource CT 2026 rate article, secondary).
credit_rollover: Netting: monetary on-bill credits carry forward month to month indefinitely and offset customer, supply and delivery charges; cash-out only when the account is closed. Buy-All: accumulated bill credits cash-out available annually on request (from 1-year anniversary of approval to operate).
annual_true_up: None for Netting (indefinite rollover, cash-out at account close). Buy-All annual cash-out option.
ic_standard: Latest IEEE 1547 series; UL 1741 SB required for applications on/after 2023-01-01 (EDCs may delay for supply-chain reasons); ISO-NE source requirement document for trip/ride-through settings
ic_fast_track_kw: 2000 (Fast Track: residential inverters >25 kW (Eversource page says >50 kW) and C&I <=2 MW passing screens)
ic_simplified_kw: 25 (residential single-phase certified inverter-based, aggregate nameplate kW AC; storage AC capacity counts toward this interconnection level)
ic_application_fee: <=25 kW certified inverter: $200. Fast Track (0-2 MW): $500. Study Process (>2 MW): $1,000 plus actual study cost. RRES application fee $129 (2022 example) separate from interconnection fee. Production meter fees (Eversource $230-$282; UI $181-$274).
ic_study_trigger_kw: 2000 (Study Process >2 MW or screen failure in Fast Track)
external_disconnect: Required - manual, lockable, gang-operated visible-break AC Isolation Device outdoors within 10 ft of the utility meter for generating facilities >1 kW unless waived in writing by the EDC; all Netting and Buy-All systems must have an AC disconnect grouped with the production meter
insurance_required: <=25 kW residential: EDC does not require insurance (customer holds EDC harmless). Fast Track/Study: minimum liability $300,000 (0-100 kW), $1M (100 kW-1 MW), $2M (1-5 MW), $5M (>5 MW) (Eversource CT)
ic_timeline_days: <=25 kW: 3 BD acknowledge, 10 BD completeness, contingent approval within 15 BD after tariff-compliance approval; 10 BD for inspection/witness after inspector approval. Fast Track: 15 BD initial review. Study: 105-120 BD.
storage_allowed: Yes - energy storage is a 'Generating Facility' under the CT guidelines; paired storage allowed under RRES (does not count toward 25 kW RRES cap but does count toward interconnection level). Retrofit: a battery added to an existing net-metered or RRES system must go through interconnection as storage only (no new RRES application if no solar added), must be located behind the existing inverter and/or not increase the effective system AC size (RRES FAQ Q68); legacy NM customers keep NM until PV is removed (Q72) - adding storage does not by itself end legacy NM on that basis. RRES does not preclude battery discharge to the grid (Q70). ESS program requires residential batteries be export-capable unless exempted.
grid_charging_allowed: Unclear - no CT rule located that prohibits or permits grid charging of a battery paired with a Netting or legacy NM system; the RRES manual and FAQ are silent. Netting credits are computed on the net of the bi-directional revenue meter, and the REC incentive on a separate PV production meter, so grid-charged discharge would net against the revenue meter; no explicit crediting rule found. ESS program (Active Dispatch) compensation is performance-based and does not address charging source in the text read.
non_export_option: Unclear - self-consumption/no-export systems must still go through interconnection (RRES FAQ Q15); flexible interconnection proposals pending in Docket 25-01-27. Defined relay-based non-export path not verified.
storage_counts_toward_cap: No (for RRES 25 kW AC cap) / Yes for interconnection review level (RRES Manual Sec. N and fn. 31)
